prerequisites: Competencies taught in the basic modules of Computer Science, and the advanced modules Software Engineering and Software Practicum are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: explain the paradigm of model-driven software development
model and develop application software in a model-driven way
explain core concepts and techniques of model-driven development
discuss the possibilities and limitations of model-driven software development
have a basic understanding of the tools presented in the course and their practical application
apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating, and solving problems
speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion

syllabus_topics: Modeling software at a higher level of abstraction using a domain-specific language
Application of existing domain-specific languages and code generators
Techniques and tools for developing new languages and generators

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercise assignments (at least 50% of points)
Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise assignments
Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: Grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program. To acquire the credits, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution of at least two of the exercise assignments. The examination performance will be an oral examination or a written exam.
